title: prevent-sse-heartbeat-coalescing-and-add-span-markers-for-partial_json
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Clients intermittently fail to parse streamed JSON payloads when keep-alive heartbeats from the platform are coalesced with payload chunks. Root cause analysis showed that two independent issues combined: (1) keep-alive comments used the same colon-delimited framing as payload events and could be merged into the same TCP chunk, producing sequences like '\n: \ndata: {"choices": ...' which some parsers treat as a single event, and (2) partial JSON payloads that span chunk boundaries lacked an explicit lightweight span marker, forcing the client to rely on heuristics and occasionally produce truncated or duplicate tokens. What this PR does: introduces explicit lightweight span markers (span:start/span:continue/span:end) as optional pseudo-events for partial JSON reassembly, changes the keep-alive heartbeat to emit a distinguishable comment token (׳::hb::׳) that cannot collide with 'data:' framing, and hardens the server-side coalescer to never merge heartbeat tokens into adjacent data events. The compatibility layer translates these pseudo-events back to standard SSE 'data:' frames for older clients unless the client signals support via the new 'SSE-Span-Support: 1' header. The change is feature-flagged and backwards-compatible by default. Impact: reduces parse errors in streaming edge cases (kept partial JSON, duplicate close braces) and makes instrumentation (span-level reassembly metrics) available for debugging. Rollout plan: feature-flag rollout to 20% of traffic for two days, monitor streaming parse errors and end-to-end token continuity metrics, then 100% if stable. Testing: added unit tests for parser state transitions, integration tests against browser EventSource harness plus Node streaming consumers, and an end-to-end replay fixture that previously reproduced the customer-reported failure. See linked Linear tasks for the incident and follow-ups.
commit_summary: [pr] heartbeat: use distinct token for keep-alive; [pr] add span markers and parser handlers; [test] add e2e replay harness; [ci] adjust dockerfiles for test harness; [docs] SSE compat note
changes_summary: Primary changes: introduce span marker pseudo-events and parser support; change heartbeat framing token; prevent coalescing of heartbeat with data in the coalescer; add header-based opt-in and backward compatibility translation; add unit + e2e tests; update docs.
review_comments: Evan Marshall (reviewer): I reproduced the issue locally with the replay fixture — good find. Two asks: document the opt-in header behavior clearly and ensure metric labels include the span-id to make postmortems easier.
Priya Nair (author): Added SSE-Span-Support header docs and included span_id in reassembly metrics. Also added a short migration note in docs/compat/sse-span-markers.md.

Diego Morales (reviewer): Concern: will older SDKs choke on the new pseudo-events if a proxy rewrites headers? Suggest we fallback to classic 'data:' frames at the edge when the header isn't present. Also please add a small benchmark for coalescer overhead.
Priya Nair (author): Implemented edge fallback (translate span pseudo-events -> data:) and added a microbenchmark that shows <1% additional CPU under heavy streaming. Bench details in commit 3.

Liam Chen (approver): Verified e2e against Node and Chrome EventSource. CI was flaky on first run (integration timeout) but passed after increasing timeout. Approving for squash merge with the documented rollback plan.
release_notes: Fix: Prevent SSE keep-alive heartbeats from being coalesced into payload events, add optional span markers for robust partial-JSON reassembly, and add header-based opt-in for clients. Backwards-compatible by default.
notes_on_rollout: Feature-flagged rollout: start at 20% traffic for 48 hours, check streaming-parse-errors and token-continuity (span_reassembly_failures < 0.1%), then 100%. If regressions, flip flag back and roll to 100% previous config.
hotfix_reference: SUP-2312 incident replay attached; this PR contains the permanent fix following the hotpatch applied during incident triage.
extra_context: Related work: this approach differs from previous 'sentinel' changes by keeping heartbeats semantic and lightweight while providing explicit reassembly hints; it enables targeted telemetry without changing the downstream payload semantics when the header is absent.
